characterList.description: A Black woman with dark hair in a bun, wearing a black t-shirt with a volleyball design and black athletic pants. She is the main character and the coach providing instructions.
characterList.name: Coach Koko

characterList.description: A man with long dark hair and a beard, wearing a white t-shirt and blue shorts. He assists Coach Koko in the partner drills.
characterList.name: Male Partner

content_metadata.description: A volleyball training video hosted by Coach Koko, focused on self-passing techniques and partner drills.

qAndA.answer: Level 1 is self-passing, setting, and catching. Level 2 is self-passing, setting, and doing a roll shot.
qAndA.question: What two levels are there to the self-passing drill that Coach Koko demonstrates?

qAndA.answer: Coach Koko explains that minimizing body movements helps players develop accurate passing and setting skills by relying on platform control rather than excessive adjustments.
qAndA.question: Why does Coach Koko emphasize minimizing body movements during the self-passing drill?

qAndA.answer: He gives her a free ball, which is a toss that allows her to easily receive the ball without much movement.
qAndA.question: In the partner drill, what type of toss does Coach Koko's fiancé initially give her?

qAndA.answer: By practicing each skill in isolation, players can focus on improving specific techniques before combining them into a fluid sequence.
qAndA.question: What is the purpose of breaking down the self-passing drill into individual skills?

qAndA.answer: The concluding scene showcases Coach Koko's personal growth in passing and emphasizes the importance of consistent practice and knowledge sharing for improvement in volleyball.
qAndA.question: How does the video's concluding scene contribute to the overall message?

activities.description: Explaining the importance of controlling the volleyball and introducing the concept of self-passing complete.
Demonstrating the two levels of self-passing drill: self-passing and catch, and self-passing and roll shot.
Emphasizing the importance of maintaining the ball in "space" and minimizing body adjustments.
Focusing on level 1 ball control (self-passing, setting, and catching) for building a foundation and minimizing movements.
Encouraging viewers to practice the level 1 drill repeatedly.
Transitioning to level 2 ball control (self-passing, setting, and roll shot) and explaining its increased difficulty.

keyMoments.changeDescription: The mood shifts slightly to become more challenging, as Coach Koko acknowledges the increased difficulty of level 2.

narrativeProgression.description: Coach Koko explains the concept of self-passing complete and demonstrates two levels of a self-passing drill. She encourages viewers to practice for mastery.

scenes.thematicElements: Ball control, platform technique, accuracy in passing and setting
scenes.title: Self-Passing Explanation and Demonstration

videoEditingDetails.description: Text overlay "Needs: Yourself, Open Space, Volleyball".
Animated text overlay "SELF PASSING COMPLETE".
Text overlay "Self Passing + Set + Catch = Level 1 Ball Control".
Text overlay "Practice it several times until you feel comfortable and competent to get the ball this way."
Text overlay "REPETITIVE PASSING [SELF]".
Text overlay "Remember that we want to have as little body adjustments as possible. We want to get used to passing/setting accurately."

activities.description: Explaining the importance of self-passing for controlling the ball and understanding its movement in space.
Highlighting the importance of practicing self-setting, acknowledging it as more challenging.
Breaking down the self-passing drill into individual skills for isolated practice.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Breaking down the skills involved in self-passing.

narrativeProgression.description: Coach Koko explains why mastering self-passing is crucial for volleyball. She demonstrates self-setting and encourages viewers to practice this challenging skill. She then advises practicing individual components before putting them all together.

scenes.thematicElements: Skill development, target practice, understanding ball movement
scenes.title: Importance of Self-Passing and Individual Skill Breakdown

videoEditingDetails.description: Text overlay "ADDING ROLL SHOTS".
Text overlay "Next, work on self-setting (this may be much more challenging)."
Text overlay "Let's now put those individual skills together in a sequence to see if we are seeing some changes to the complete sequence."

activities.description: Challenging viewers to complete the self-passing sequence non-stop.
Transitioning to partner drills for self-reception.
Introducing partner drills and explaining the setup (partner, open space).
Demonstrating self-reception with a free ball toss from the partner.
Increasing the difficulty with down ball tosses from the partner.

characterInteraction.description: Coach Koko directs her male partner to provide the tosses for her self-reception practice.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Introduction of partner drills adds a more interactive and game-like atmosphere, simulating real-game scenarios.

narrativeProgression.description: Coach Koko challenges viewers to perform the self-passing sequence continuously. She introduces partner drills for practicing self-reception. She demonstrates receiving free balls and down balls.

scenes.thematicElements: Partner practice, receiving serves, game simulation
scenes.title: Level 2 Challenge and Self-Reception with a Partner

videoEditingDetails.description: Text overlay "SELF RECEPTION".
Text overlay "Self Passing + Set + Roll Shot + Catch = Level 2".

Text overlay "Needs: Partner, Volleyball, Open Space"

activities.description: Sharing her personal experience of working on passing skills.
Encouraging viewers to practice and share the video.
Saying goodbye and ending the video.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Encouragement to continue learning and practicing.

narrativeProgression.description: Coach Koko concludes the video by encouraging viewers to practice and improve their passing skills.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Hey, what's up you guys welcome back to my channel my name is coach Coco and I love volleyball so much though
My channel is for a tips tricks hacks and anything you can ever need to know about volleyball so today. Let's talk about self-passing
Have you ever heard the old saying that you have to control the ball and now let the ball control you?
Well, that is some true facts. Today, let's work on self-passing and how to increase our chances of passing with success.
You need yourself an open space and a volleyball.
Now there's a lot of different ways that you can self pass but first let's talk about what self-passing complete is.
The first thing you want to do is you want to make sure that you have your platform, you're going to set it to yourself and then roll shot it.
That is a complete self-pass. There are two levels to this drill, the self-passing and catch and then the self-passing and roll shot.
To start off the level one ball control, we're going to self-pass it to ourselves, set it and then catch it.
This is going to build the foundation for us to start learning how to pass to ourselves with control with minimal movements.
You want to make sure that you're focusing on your platform, you want to also make sure that we want to keep the ball in our space and we want to have little body adjustment.
We want to be able to start passing it to ourselves repetitively without us moving a whole bunch.
Practice several times until you feel comfortable and competent to get the ball this way.
Then once we start finishing that we're going to move forward.
Remember that we want to move our body as little as possible because we want to set and pass it.
Here we're going to take it to the next level.
Now you're going to start to pass repetitively. That means over and over again.
We want to have little body movements and we want to keep it on target and receive the ball.
This does take some practice so we're going to work on it.
So you might be thinking, how is this skill important?
It's important because we have to be able to control the ball more passing to a target and we want to be able to receive the ball and understand how the ball moves in space.
Now let's break down each part individually. After we've passed it repetitively then you're going to set to yourself.
Now this might be a little challenging for some people because if you're not a setter it's going to take a little bit of time.
But once you get each of those parts individually then go back to that past, set and catch.
See how much better you do when you break down each piece individually before putting it together.
Now here's for my big ballers. If you're ready to go at past set and then roll shot go ahead do your level two.
Past set and roll shot. Now you're not going to roll shot it like to a target across from you.
You're going to do a light roll shot and catch it.
You're going to see yourself move a little bit more here because roll shots tend to be a little bit uncontrolled but that's where we're working on.
Just roll it straight back down. We want to be serious and if you want to be serious go non-stop.
This is a hard challenge. Even for me it's a challenge but it keeps you going and it's one way to keep your number one your volleyball stamina up.
But it also helps keep your volleyball eye ready.
Now once you've gotten this self passing drill down you're going to need a partner and I'm using my fiancee here.
You need a partner a volleyball and an open space. What you guys are going to do is you're going to arrange yourself so that way they can toss the ball to you.
The first thing they're going to do is give you a free ball and then you're going to try to receive that ball but you're going to pass it to yourself.
No hands on the knees ready position then you're going to give it back. You're going to receive it to yourself and then give it back.
I know a lot of times we have difficulty getting the ball to the center so just make sure that you're trying to keep your body control trying not to fall down.
And we're trying to make sure that we have that passing control that we need. Now if you need to ramp it up you can do a down ball.
Teach a partner if they've never played before what a down ball is. Same thing you want to try to control it as much as you can.
It might be a little bit more difficult depending on how hard your partner is hitting but you want to receive it as well as you can.
This is the type of ball that you can start getting to a target. Give it back to your partner but you want to make sure that it's something that they can set.
We're not getting a ball that shoots out but a ball that they can set. When I was playing high school volleyball I was not a passer and I did not pay black row.
So passing is something that I had to work on at length. I want you to make sure that you are using your correct platform, that your body position is correct and your eyes can see the ball.
And I want you to just take your time. Practice does make improvement and we have to practice the skills that we struggle with the most in order to get better.
Passing was not one of my stronger skills but it's getting better now. So I hope this volleyball video really helped you with yourself passing and that you liked it.
Share it with somebody who needs it and I will see you guys next time.
